newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand may export palm oil, stocks at 112,995T.
newsitem.headline: Thailand may export palm oil, stocks at 112,995T.

text.p: The Thai government may export crude palm oil to get rid of excessive stock which is standing at 112,995 tonnes, a 117 percent rise from the same period last year, a commerce ministry source said on Friday.
Some 41,140 tonnes of stock are detailed as being at extraction factories, 53,155 tonnes at refineries and 18,700 tonnes at the commerce ministry's Public Warehouse Organisation.
"We might export some of that to reduce the stock ahead of the peak harvesting season in May. Otherwise, the prices of local palm could be pressured," the source said.
But the official declined to say how much palm oil the government plans to export and to whom.
The ministry's stock figure for refineries differed slightly from the one estimated by the industry.
Somsak Kositset of Thai Palm Oil Refinery Association told Reuters on Wednesday that the stock held by refineries was about 60,000-70,000 tonnes.
The commerce ministry source said the government will soon review the demand-supply situation for November-February which is a low harvesting season for palm.
"But it is unlikely that there will be any need for crude palm oil imports for next year," he said.
Thai palm oil refineries imported about 25,000 tonnes of the crude product this year.
